title: The Foxes of Elm Road
subtitle: A city street agreed to be studied, and learned something about its neighbours
text: Two years ago, every household on Elm Road received the same letter. A research group at the university wanted to study the urban foxes living in the area, and needed permission to place small cameras in back gardens. {0} Within a month, thirty-one of the forty-two houses had agreed.

The foxes had been there far longer than the cameras. Residents had been arguing about them for years, mostly at a distance and mostly without evidence. {1} The recordings settled several of these disputes in a single afternoon.

One early finding surprised almost everyone. The street had assumed it was dealing with a large population passing through. {2} They were the same four animals, night after night, using the same six gardens.
The cameras also showed how narrow a fox's world can be. {3} Numbers 14 and 16 were visited constantly; number 18, two doors along, was never entered once in eleven months.

What the residents made of the footage turned out to be more interesting than the footage itself. The people who had complained loudest about the foxes were the ones who watched the recordings most closely. {4} One of them now keeps a written record of arrivals and departures.
The study finished last spring and the cameras came down. {5} Several households asked whether they could buy the equipment and carry on alone.
The foxes, as far as anyone can tell, have not noticed that the study is over. {6}
sentences: Some were convinced there were dozens of them; others insisted they had never seen one at all.
Two of the original four are still using the same route across the same gardens, at roughly the same hour each night.
Foxes are known to travel several kilometres in a single night when food is difficult to find.
Their routes are fixed to a degree that surprised even the researchers.
In return, the group promised to share everything it recorded with the street.
It is much harder to dislike an animal you have watched for any length of time.
In fact, the footage from all thirty-one gardens showed nothing of the kind.
The reaction of the street was not at all what the researchers had expected.
